He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]], earning [[Big 12 Conference]] Freshman of the Year in 2023. George was selected by the Jazz with the 16th overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]]. He is the son of former professional basketball player [[Jason Siggers]]. ==Early life== George began playing high school basketball for [[Lewisville High School]] in [[Lewisville, Texas]].{{cite web|last=Bossi|first=Eric|title=Class of 2022 Keyonte George has KU, Texas, others on radar|url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/class-of-2022-keyonte-george-has-ku-texas-others-on-radar|website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]]|access-date=September 17, 2021|date=December 6, 2019}} As a freshman, he averaged 21 points, four rebounds and 1.9 steals per game, and was named District 6-6A Offensive Player of the Year.{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Justin|title=The best on the basketball court: Locals named to 6-6A all-district team|url=https://starlocalmedia.com/carrolltonleader/sports/the-best-on-the-basketball-court-locals-named-to-6-6a-all-district-team/article_0624213e-45b4-11e9-bb91-7395a468ab24.html|website=Carrollton Leader|access-date=September 17, 2021|date=March 13, 2019}} George averaged 23.9 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 2.1 steals per game as a sophomore, earning District 6-6A MVP honors. For his junior season, he transferred to iSchool of Lewisville.{{cite web|last=Riddle|first=Greg|title=Five-star basketball recruit Keyonte George is transferring from Lewisville to iSchool of Lewisville|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2020/05/01/five-star-basketball-recruit-keyonte-george-is-transferring-from-lewisville-to-ischool-of-lewisville/|website=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|access-date=September 17, 2021|date=May 1, 2020}} George averaged 24.8 points per game as a junior.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author-link2=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=August 8, 2021 |title=Top-five 2022 prospect Keyonte George commits to Baylor Bears |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31988003 |access-date=September 17, 2021 |website=[[ESPN]]}} He moved to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]] for his senior season,{{cite web|last=Divens|first=Jordan|title=High school basketball: Keyonte George, Dior Johnson and Mikey Williams among impact transfers|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/2ctu0sgTGEybI-F803qWNw/high-school-basketball--keyonte-george,-dior-johnson-and-mikey-williams-among-impact-transfers.htm|website=[[MaxPreps]]|access-date=September 17, 2021|date=September 2, 2021}} where he averaged 17.8 points per game and shot 41% from three-point range. He was the highest-ranked recruit in program history when he committed to Baylor University for the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023 college basketball season]].{{Cite web |date=2023-06-23 |title=IMG Academy Sets Basketball Program Record After Three Alumni Selected in the First Round of the 2023 NBA Draft |url=https://www.imgacademy.com/news/img-academy-sets-basketball-program-record-after-three-alumni-selected-first-round-2023-nba |access-date=2023-07-30 |website=IMG Academy |language=en}} George was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. On August 8, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] over offers from [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2022}} {{College basketball team|West Virginia]].{{cite news|title=George scores 32, Baylor beats West Virginia 83–78|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401493393|access-date=March 6, 12|url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/flagler-named-first-team-all-big-12/article_99f8d02c-bba2-11ed-af41-6bdce25ad8ae.html|access-date=March 6, 2023|work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]]|date=March 5, 2023}} George scored 506 points as a freshman at Baylor, the second most in school history, and holds the program record for the most 20-point games in program history with 20.{{Cite web |date=2023-06-23 |title=IMG Academy Sets Basketball Program Record After Three Alumni Selected in the First Round of the 2023 NBA Draft |url=https://www.imgacademy.com/news/img-academy-sets-basketball-program-record-after-three-alumni-selected-first-round-2023-nba |access-date=2023-07-30 |website=IMG Academy |language=en}} ==Professional career== The [[Utah Jazz]] selected George with the sixteenth overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2023/06/22/utah-jazz-select-baylor-guard/|title=Utah Jazz select Baylor guard Keyonte George at No. 16|last=Larsen|first=Andy|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 24, 2023}} After playing [[shooting guard]] as a prep and in college, George began playing as a [[point guard]] under head coach [[Will Hardy]].{{Cite web |last=Todd |first=Sarah |date=2024-03-03 |title=Utah Jazz: Keyonte George continuing to find his voice |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/03/02/utah-jazz-keyonte-george-still-learning-his-way-during-rookie-season/ |access-date=2024-03-03 |website=Deseret News |language=en}} On October 25, 2023, George made his NBA regular season debut against the [[Sacramento Kings]], putting up eight points, two rebounds, and two assists off the bench in a 130–114 loss.{{Cite web |last=Kostecka |first=Ryan |date=2023-10-26 |title="I Feel Like I Belong" — Confidence And Preparation Led To A Successful NBA Debut For George |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/i-feel-like-i-belong-confidence-and-preparation-led-to-a-successful-nba-debut-for-george |access-date=2023-11-21 |website=nba.com}} On December 2, George scored a then career high 21 points against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], adding six rebounds and six assists in the game.{{cite web | last=Koch | first=Jared | title=Keyonte George Posts Stellar Season-High Performance vs. Trail Blazers | website=Yardbarker | date=2023-12-03 | url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/keyonte_george_posts_stellar_season_high_performance_vs_trail_blazers/s1_16742_39620272 | access-date=2025-12-06}} On December 12, George scored a new career-high 30 points against the [[2023–24 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |date=2023-12-12 |title=Jazz's Keyonte George: Delivers career-high 30 points |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-keyonte-george-delivers-career-high-30-points/ |access-date=2023-12-21 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} On February 4, 2024, George recorded his first career double-double with 19 points and 10 rebounds in a 123–108 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |date=2023-02-04 |title=Jazz's Keyonte George: Posts double-double off bench |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-keyonte-george-posts-double-double-off-bench/ |access-date=2024-02-04 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} On November 4, 2024, George tied his career-high of 35 points against the [[Chicago Bulls]]. While some speculate that George was benched due to being surpassed by Collier, the move of Collier to the starting lineup allowed Keyonte to return to his role of an off-ball scorer, where he has been thriving.{{Cite web|title=Jazz lose to Bucks, but say moving Collier to a starter is 'best for team' right now|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/51238922/jazz-lose-to-bucks-but-say-moving-collier-to-a-starter-is-best-for-team-right-now|access-date=January 27, 2025|website=ksl.com|language=en}} On December 15, 2025, George recorded 37 points, four rebounds, and six assists in a 140-133 overtime victory over the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|title=George scores 37 as Jazz top Mavericks in OT despite Flagg's career-high 42|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/51419769/george-scores-37-as-jazz-top-mavericks-in-ot-despite-flaggs-career-high-42|access-date=February 26, 2026|website=ksl.com|language=en}} On January 20, 2026, George recorded a career-high 43 points in a 127–122 victory over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite news |last=Liebert |first=Tony |title=Wolves Can't Slow Down Keyonte George in Road Loss to Jazz |url=https://www.si.com/nba/timberwolves/onsi/minnesota-timberwolves-news/wolves-can-t-slow-down-keyonte-george-in-road-loss-to-jazz |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=January 20, 2026 |access-date=February 28, 2026}} He scored 25 points in the first half alone and finished the game shooting 15-of-28 from the field, including six three-pointers.{{cite web |title=George's career-high 43 points lifts Jazz past Timberwolves at home |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/51435995/georges-career-high-43-points-lifts-jazz-past-timberwolves-at-home |publisher=KSL.com |date=January 20, 2026 |access-date=February 28, 2026}} With this performance, George recorded his seventh game of the season with at least 30 points and five three-pointers, tying [[Bojan Bogdanović]] for the third-most such games in a single season in Jazz history.{{cite web |title=Keyonte George Explodes For Career-High 43 PTS |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Pfr2XHHLCE |website=YouTube |publisher=NBA |date=January 20, 2026 |access-date=February 28, 2026}} ==National team career== George represented the [[United States men's national under-18 3x3 team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA 3x3 U18 World Cup – Men's tournament|2021 FIBA 3x3 Under-18 World Cup]] in [[Debrecen]], Hungary. He won the gold medal with his teammates: [[Kyle Filipowski]], [[Gradey Dick]] and [[Eric Dailey Jr.]] George was named World Cup MVP after averaging a tournament-high 8.2 points per game.{{cite web|title=USA Men Claim First Back-to-Back Gold at FIBA 3x3 U18 World Cup|url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2021/08/3x3-mu18-wc-aug-29.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830134659/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2021/08/3x3-mu18-wc-aug-29.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=August
